chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Ibrahim ibn Shaybah, who said:

I wrote to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) asking him about the prayer behind the one who holds the authority of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), while he considers wiping over the two socks (khuffayn) valid, or behind the one who prohibits wiping over the socks while he himself wipes. He replied: 'If a place unites you and them, and you find no alternative but to pray, then give the call to prayer (adhan) for yourself and establish the prayer (iqamah). If they precede you in the recitation, then glorify (say Subhanallah).'

key_terms.أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (referring to the Imams)
key_terms.الْمَسْحَ عَلَى الْخُفَّيْنِ: Wiping over the two socks (a method of ablution)

ai.seo_question: How should one pray behind an Imam who differs inerrant Imam who holds a different view on a minor ritual detail like wiping over socks?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* addresses the practical jurisprudence of praying behind an Imam whose minor ritual difference (such as wiping over socks) does not invalidate the prayer, emphasizing unity over sectarian rigidity. It provides a specific procedural solution—performing one's own Adhan and Iqamah—to maintain congregational cohesion when no alternative Imam is available, reflecting the Shia principle of *al-jama'ah* (congregation) even in the presence of differing *fiqh* opinions. This highlights the flexibility within Shia jurisprudence regarding secondary details (*furū'*) while preserving the validity of the prayer behind the designated leader.
